data.narrative:
Duranium is a pre-seed stage climate and energy company founded by Berkley Noble and Brenden Prins-McKinney. The Climate & Energy sector comprises a fragmented peer set of nine private companies and one public comparable (LNZA). Top private peers include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, extracting valuation guidance from this universe proves constrained: no pre-seed or adjacent-stage peers exist in sufficient density to support median-based triangulation, and similar-valuation-tier filtering yielded insufficient overlap.

Given $2M in total capital raised to date, the Stage-Progression method is applicable and supplies the primary valuation signal. Using a standard pre-seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x applied to the $2M raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $5M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, centered on $5M. This reflects the mechanical application of stage-progression mechanics absent robust peer-level corroboration. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables, which limits cross-validation of the step-up multiple and introduces material estimation risk. Any material shift in the founder's capitalization or commercial progress would warrant recalibration of both the base proxy and the applicable multiple.
